sounds: 你 nǐ (you, in slang such as 520)
0.mean: Wholeness, a complete circle, a fresh start

1.mean: Unity, being first, and also 'want/will' (yāo ≈ 要)

2.mean: Ease, love and pairs: 好事成双, good things come in pairs
2.cmean: 易 'easy', a helper digit (28 = easy prosperity, 24 = easy death)

3.mean: Life and growth. Avoid it in wedding gifts, where 散 means 'split'
3.cmean: 生 'life, alive': strongly positive in Cantonese

4.mean: Sounds like 死 'death'. It is the most avoided digit: buildings skip 4th floors and plates with 4 sell cheaply

5.mean: 'Me' in slang, and the five elements (五行). Neutral to mildly positive
5.cmean: 唔 m̀ 'not': it negates the next digit (54 = won't die, 58 = won't prosper)

6.mean: Smoothness and flow: 六六大顺, everything goes smoothly

7.mean: Rising, togetherness and romance (七夕, Qixi, is Chinese Valentine's Day). Mixed in some combos (7456, 748)
7.cmean: A vulgar slang homophone in Cantonese: use with care in HK and Guangdong

8.mean: The king of lucky numbers, 发 'prosperity'. The Beijing Olympics opened 08/08/08 at 8:08 pm
8.cmean: 發 faat 'prosper': the most lucky digit

9.mean: Longevity and eternity: 天长地久. Historically linked with the emperor
9.cmean: 久 'long-lasting': positive (a few slang uses are coarse)

entries.pinyin: èr qī líng èr qī líng
entries.en: Our namesake: an ABCABC mirror number. Folk readings are 'easy rise, bright spirit', doubled (好事成双), and the romantic 爱妻你 'love, wife, you'. It contains no 4.

entries.pinyin: wǔ èr líng ≈ wǒ ài nǐ
entries.en: I love you. 20 May (5/20) is China's Internet Valentine's Day, with record marriage registrations and gift sales
I'm willing / I do. A reply to 520, and 21 May is another romantic date

entries.pinyin: wǔ sān líng ≈ wǒ xiǎng nǐ
entries.en: I miss you

entries.pinyin: yī sān yī sì ≈ yīshēng yīshì
entries.en: For a whole lifetime, forever. Common on wedding red envelopes (e.g. ¥1314)
I love you forever. The classic romantic transfer amount (¥520.1314)

entries.pinyin: jiǔ sì èr líng ≈ jiùshì ài nǐ
entries.en: It's you I love, just you

entries.pinyin: sān sān sì sì ≈ shēngshēng shìshì
entries.en: Life after life, eternally. It shows how 4 can turn positive in context

entries.pinyin: sān sān jiǔ jiǔ ≈ chángcháng jiǔjiǔ

Kiss you

Forever and ever. 999 roses mean eternal love
Eternal, everlasting (999 roses, 999 gold)
Prosperity: the single luckiest digit

entries.en: Prosperity × 3. The most popular lucky price and phone ending
Ultimate prosperity. Sichuan Airlines paid ¥2.33M for +86 28 8888 8888

Prosper and prosper all the way

I will prosper greatly
About to prosper. Also used online as 'come on, you can do it'

Will prosper (Cantonese 實發 'sure to prosper'). The HK plate '18' sold for HK$16.5M (2008)

Awesome, you're a pro! A gamer and live-stream compliment, NOT 'evil' as in the West
Super awesome; smooth sailing
Long-lasting, eternal
Lasting prosperity: a lucky alternative to Western '.99' pricing
Smooth road to wealth: a very common price ending (¥68, $68)
LOL, laughing out loud (from Mop.com emoji #233). 2333333 means ROFL
Bye-bye (chat sign-off)
